newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Central unit buys rail lines.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Central unit buys rail lines.

text.p: Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp said Tuesday its Sault Ste. Marie Bridge Co subsidiary completed its purchase of 220 route miles of track in Wisconsin and Upper Michigan for $85 million, subject to certain final adjustments.
The track was purchased from Union Pacific Corp's Union Pacific Railway Co.

The lines acquired, known as Duck Creek North, include contiguous property and associated facilities from North Green Bay, Wis., to Ishpeming, Mich.; from Powers to Antoine, Mich.; from Quinnesec, Mich., to Niagara, Wis., and from Cascade to Palmer, Mich.
The lines carry materials for the paper industry and high volumes of iron ore used in steel-making.
Wisconsin Central, which has begun operating the lines, said about 120 employees were hired initially by Sault Ste. Marie to operate the new lines, most of whom came from the Union Pacific.
